input.question: An English speaker in 2016 can understand a 200 year old book from 1816 with relative ease. Would An English speaker from 1816 be able to understand Shakespeare's then 200 year old plays just as easily?
input.ground_truth: It's unlikely, but only because Shakespeare's locution wasn't customary in his time, but peculiar even then (source: any introduction to a recent edition of a Shakespeare work). If you were to switch this question to some other author of the same period, though, I'm not sure. Edit: I also want to challenge the claim that we can understand texts from 1816 with relative ease. Academics can, but can most English speakers really deal with the crazy punctuation, tortuously long sentences, and GRE-level vocabulary?

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: An English speaker in 2016 can understand a 200 year old book from 1816 with relative ease. Would An English speaker from 1816 be able to understand Shakespeare's then 200 year old plays just as easily?

response.prediction:
Okay, let's imagine you have a toy from 20 years ago. You can still play with it, and you know what it is because toys don't change that much.

Now, let's talk about words and stories. Imagine you are a grown-up in 2016, and you find a book from 1816. Even though it's old, the words are kind of like the toys—they're not *that* different. Some words might sound funny or old-fashioned, but you can still read and understand the story pretty well, because the English language doesn't change super fast.

But if you were a grown-up in 1816, and you found a play that was written 200 years before that (so, from 1616, like Shakespeare's time), the words and the way people talked would be very, very different! It would be like trying to understand a story written in a secret code or in a different language. Some words wouldn't even be the same, and the way people said things was totally different.

So, it's easier for us to read old books from 200 years ago than it would have been for people back then to read books from 200 years before them. Time makes things harder to understand the further back you go!
